title: Canonical tensor-dual evaluation for a finite free retract
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and suppose additive-group sheafification exists and $J$-local equivalences of additive-group presheaves are exactly locally bijective maps. Use the category of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and canonical tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Let $E,B$ be module sheaves and assume there exist $m\geq0$ and maps $i:E\to R^{\oplus m}$, $p:R^{\oplus m}\to E$ with $p\circ i=1_E$. Put $E^\vee=\mathcal Hom(E,R)$. Then the canonical evaluation comparison $B\otimes E^\vee\to\mathcal Hom(E,B)$ sending $b\otimes\phi$ to $(e\mapsto b\phi(e))$ is an isomorphism. The map is the adjunct of the composite $E\otimes(B\otimes E^\vee)\to B\otimes(E^\vee\otimes E)\to B\otimes R\to B$ using symmetry, associativity, evaluation and the right unit action. No flatness or quasi-coherence is assumed of $B$.

proof.text: For E free of rank m, use the canonical finite-sum Hom identifications and coordinate equations of lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact (take the split sequence B --id--> B --> 0). Tensoring B with the free dual gives the finite coproduct of m copies of B. Evaluate the comparison on each basis vector: the j-th projection and i-th inclusion compose to id_B when i=j and zero otherwise. The finite biproduct identification therefore makes the comparison the identity, and supplies its inverse. This includes m=0.

Precomposition with p and i induces retractions on Hom(E,R) and Hom(E,B); their composites are identities because p composed with i is the identity on E. Naturality of the tensor-Hom equivalence makes the free comparison a map between these split idempotents. Its inverse commutes with the idempotents by composing the naturality equality with the free inverse. Project that inverse from the free Hom to B tensor the dual of E. Both composites are identities by the retraction equation.
